shared_elements: anthropomorphic figure rendered in low relief
raised curvilinear outlines with plain infill
justification: Both surfaces carry raised, rounded low-relief curvilinear motifs of the same repertoire: a prominent ring/disc, crescent-like arcs, and schematic hands with elongated splayed fingers attached to anthropomorphic bodies, which is a fairly specific shared vocabulary. The biggest difference in content is the organisation and subject framing: A is a single frontal anthropomorphic body whose motifs are ordered symmetrically down a vertical axis (headdress band, arms converging on a central ring, belt line), while B is a horizontally spread crowd of overlapping creature-like heads and limbs with no single dominant figure or symmetry.
